tasks.spec:
You are an Elixir engineer closing parity gaps between Cornerman's `lint` command and the Python original, byte for byte. Your current working directory IS a git worktree of the Cornerman repo, an Elixir/OTP port of the Ringer agent-swarm tool. `bin/cornerman lint` already passes the existing conformance suite; twelve new conformance cases fail and your job is to make them pass without breaking the rest.

NEVER TOUCH: anything under test/ (the conformance tests are the acceptance check), DIVERGENCES.toml (the ledger of accepted differences: you may not add entries), bin/, lib/cornerman/spawn.ex, lib/cornerman/spawn/, lib/cornerman/application.ex, mix.exs, mix.lock, .git. Do not git commit, push or git add. Do not add dependencies.

OWNED PATHS (the only files you may create or edit): anything under lib/cornerman/ except the Spawn files and application.ex above, plus ./notes.md.

THE FAILING CASES (test/conformance/lint_test.exs; fixtures in test/conformance/fixtures/lint/ and test/conformance/fixtures/config/). Each compares exit status, stdout and stderr with the oracle; the program name `ringer.py` is normalised to `cornerman`.
1. `~user` expansion. Ringer calls `Path(text).expanduser()` (pathlib, /Volumes/Personal/Users/davidwilliams/.local/share/mise/installs/python/3.12.13/lib/python3.12/pathlib.py:1398, which calls posixpath.expanduser at /Volumes/Personal/Users/davidwilliams/.local/share/mise/installs/python/3.12.13/lib/python3.12/posixpath.py:256). Cornerman's `Py.expanduser` only handles `~` and `~/`. `~name` and `~name/...` must resolve to that user's real home directory (pwd.getpwnam(name).pw_dir), and an unknown user must raise Python's RuntimeError "Could not determine home directory." (so lint exits 2 with `cornerman: error: Could not determine home directory.`). Cases: lint/tilde-user-collision (`~root/o` on two tasks is absolute, so it is a write collision), lint/error-tilde-unknown-user-workdir, lint/error-tilde-unknown-user-expect-file. Requirements the tests cannot see, and which the reviewer WILL check: (a) return the real home directory, not just "user exists": Phase 2's `run` will use the resolved paths; (b) it must work on macOS, where local users live in Directory Services and are NOT all in /etc/passwd, and on Ubuntu 24.04 CI, so reading /etc/passwd alone is wrong; (c) never interpolate the user-supplied name into shell text (no `sh -c "... ~#{name}"`); if you run an external command, pass the name as a separate argv element, and say in notes.md why the command you chose is safe and portable. Check every caller of Py.expanduser / Py.resolve still behaves (workdir, repo, expect_files collision, RINGER_CONFIG path).
2. `int()` on Unicode digits. Python's int(str) strips Unicode whitespace, accepts an optional sign, and accepts ANY Unicode decimal digit (general category Nd), with single underscores between digits. Cases: lint/unicode-digit-max-parallel ("١" is 1), lint/unicode-digit-timeout (fullwidth digits with U+3000/U+2003 around them).
3. JSON NaN, Infinity, -Infinity. Python's json.loads accepts these three literals anywhere a JSON value may appear and turns them into float nan/inf/-inf; Elixir's JSON module rejects them. `Py.int` already maps :nan/:infinity/:neg_infinity to Python's messages. Cases: lint/error-nan-max-parallel ("cannot convert float NaN to integer"), lint/error-infinity-timeout, lint/nan-unused-field (NaN/Infinity in fields Ringer ignores: lint must carry on normally). Also make a numeric literal that overflows a float (e.g. 1e400) come out as inf, as Python's json does. Invalid JSON must still fail with `cornerman: error: ` plus a one-line message (the existing lint/error-invalid-json case and its DIVERGENCES.toml entry allow the message text after the prefix to differ).
4. dict repr in insertion order. Python dicts keep insertion order; Cornerman decodes JSON objects to maps and `Py.repr` prints map order. Case: lint/error-dict-repr-order (`redact_spec` set to a nested object). Hint: `JSON.decode/3` with `object_start`/`object_push`/`object_finish` decoders sees pairs in document order (verified on Elixir 1.20.1); an ordered representation that the manifest validation still reads cleanly is one option. With duplicate keys in one object, Python keeps the LAST value at the FIRST key's position. Keep validation at the boundary: rules downstream should not need to know about ordering.
5. repr and str.isprintable(). `Py.repr` approximates isprintable with a hand-written range list. Python's rule: a character is printable unless its general category is Cc, Cf, Cs, Co, Cn, Zl, Zp or Zs (space U+0020 excepted). Case: lint/error-repr-nonprintable (U+0378 unassigned, U+0600 and U+2066 and U+180E format, U+FFFF noncharacter, U+E0001 tag, U+F0000 and U+10FFFD supplementary private use; é, ก and 😀 stay literal). The oracle's Python 3.12.13 uses Unicode 15.0.0; OTP 28 ships Unicode 16.0 and has no general-category API. Generate your tables (Nd digits for item 2, non-printable ranges for item 5) from Python 3.12.13's unicodedata, compacted to ranges in an Elixir module under lib/cornerman/, with a header comment naming the Unicode version and the exact command that regenerates it. State the Unicode version in notes.md.
6. TOML inline tables. `Cornerman.TomlOrder` recovers key order by scanning the TOML text but skips keys inside inline tables, so engines declared as `engines = { zeta = {...}, alpha = {...}, mid = {...} }` print their warnings alphabetically; Python's tomllib keeps file order. Case: lint/diagnostic-inline-table-engine-order (config fixture config/inline-engines.toml). Handle inline tables at any depth, including dotted keys inside them (`engines = { zeta.bin = "z", zeta.args_template = ["{spec}"], alpha.bin = "a", ... }`), and strings containing braces, commas or `=`.
7. argparse's option-vs-value rule. `cornerman --config -x lint m` must fail like argparse: usage on stderr and `cornerman: error: argument --config: expected one argument`, exit 2. Case: lint/argv-config-value-looks-like-option. Port argparse's actual rule from /Volumes/Personal/Users/davidwilliams/.local/share/mise/installs/python/3.12.13/lib/python3.12/argparse.py (_parse_optional at line 2320, _get_option_tuples at 2366, the negative-number matcher at 1413): for instance `--config -1`, `--config '-x y'` (contains a space) and `--config=-x` are all accepted as values by argparse and must be by Cornerman, and argparse accepts unambiguous prefixes of long options (`--conf`). Apply the same rule to the lint subcommand's own arguments.

THE REFERENCE for lint itself is /Volumes/Personal/Users/davidwilliams/dev/elixir/cornerman/vendor/ringer-py/ringer.py (TaskSpec ~1725, Manifest ~1811, lint_manifest ~1901, main ~11090, AppConfig.load ~1062). Read the existing lib/cornerman modules first (cli.ex, cli/args.ex, manifest.ex, py.ex, toml_order.ex, app_config.ex, lint.ex, env.ex): they are the landed port and its conventions.

DESIGN: validate at the boundary. Parsing turns JSON and TOML into validated structs in one place; lint rules work on those structs with no error handling of their own. Small pure functions. No `try`/`rescue` for control flow where a tagged tuple will do.

SETUP (run once, first, from this directory; the sandbox cannot fetch packages and this worktree has no submodule checkout):
  cp -R /Volumes/Personal/Users/davidwilliams/dev/elixir/cornerman/deps ./deps
  export PATH=/Volumes/Personal/Users/davidwilliams/.local/share/mise/installs/elixir/1.20.1-otp-28/bin:/Volumes/Personal/Users/davidwilliams/.local/share/mise/installs/erlang/28.5/bin:/Volumes/Personal/Users/davidwilliams/.local/share/mise/installs/python/3.12.13/bin:$PATH HEX_OFFLINE=1 CORNERMAN_ORACLE=/Volumes/Personal/Users/davidwilliams/dev/elixir/cornerman/vendor/ringer-py CORNERMAN_PYTHON=/Volumes/Personal/Users/davidwilliams/.local/share/mise/installs/python/3.12.13/bin/python3

HOW TO RUN (after the setup, from this directory):
  MIX_ENV=test mix compile --warnings-as-errors
  mix format
  mix test test/conformance            # all lint parity cases; failures name the field that differs
  mix test test/conformance/lint_test.exs:<line>   # a single case
  RINGER_NO_SELF_UPDATE=1 /Volumes/Personal/Users/davidwilliams/.local/share/mise/installs/python/3.12.13/bin/python3 /Volumes/Personal/Users/davidwilliams/dev/elixir/cornerman/vendor/ringer-py/ringer.py lint <manifest>   # what the oracle prints
  /Volumes/Personal/Users/davidwilliams/.local/share/mise/installs/python/3.12.13/bin/python3 -c 'import unicodedata; print(unicodedata.unidata_version)'   # 15.0.0
Iterate until `mix test` passes in full (the phase 0 Spawn tests must stay green). Then write your own inputs for each numbered item that no fixture covers, run them through the oracle and bin/cornerman, and fix what differs: a reviewer will do the same with inputs you have not seen. The verifying check runs outside your sandbox, with the same oracle, and runs the full suite twice from clean deps.

OUTPUT CONTRACT: your changes under lib/cornerman/, formatted, compiling with no warnings, plus ./notes.md with: what you changed per numbered item and why, the Unicode version of your tables and how to regenerate them, how `~user` is resolved and why it is safe and portable, every extra input you probed against the oracle and its result, and anything your sandboxed test run could not verify.
tasks.verified: every lint conformance case, including the twelve ENG-495 gap cases, matches the pinned Ringer oracle byte for byte (twice, from clean deps, outside the sandbox); tests/ledger/launcher untouched; only lib/cornerman changed outside Spawn; formatted; no warnings.
